why: Replacing O1 made the model prefer cuts that complete the left span (clause/NP‑completing cuts) when two candidates lie in the same attachment chain, which reordered many mid-to-deep candidates and produced the small overall gain concentrated in short-latency bins (≤3, ≤5). However the change slightly weakened the single top choice (rank‑1 fell), explaining the handful of large negative tail moves even though more (and deeper) positions improved.
lesson: When adding an ‘prefer left‑span complete’ rule, target improvements to deeper candidate ranks (helping short-latency bins) without degrading the primary top‑1 cut—preserve the best early choice while reordering lower ranks.
